sample_size.excerpt: The Age-Related Eye Disease Study randomized 3,640 patients with age related macular degeneration to 1 of 4 study arms, including placebo, antioxidants (500 mg vitamin C, 400 IU vitamin E and 15 mg beta-carotene), 80 mg zinc and antioxidant plus zinc.

effect_size.excerpt: There was no increase in prostate or other cancers with zinc supplementation. A significant decrease in prostate cancer diagnoses was seen in patients receiving antioxidants vs placebo (RR = 0.6, 95% CI 0.49-0.86, p = 0.049).

validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting dietary calcium intake and incident prostate cancer risk with a multivariate relative risk estimate.

extraction.population: 29,133 male smokers aged 50-69 years in the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study

sample_size.excerpt: We examined dietary intakes of calcium and dairy products in relation to risk of prostate cancer in the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene (ATBC) Cancer Prevention Study, a cohort of 29,133 male smokers aged 50-69 years at study entry.

cases.excerpt: During 17 years of follow-up, we ascertained 1,267 incident cases of prostate cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: The multivariate relative risk (RR) of prostate cancer for > or =2,000 mg/day compared to <1,000 mg/day of calcium intake was 1.63 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.27-2.10; p trend < 0.0001).
